rules.title: Nonpayment of rent: utility payment defense
rules.requirement: A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment of rent if the tenant used the unpaid rent to keep utility services (electric, gas, water, sewer) going after notice of discontinuance, where the landlord was responsible for those utilities and did not pay. Money so used counts as part of the rent payment.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants facing eviction for nonpayment of rent where the landlord was responsible for utility payments.
rules.quoted_span: Note: A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment of rent, if the tenant used the unpaid portion of rent to continue utility services to the rental premises after receiving notice that the services were in danger of being discontinued, and if the landlord was responsible for the payment of those utility services and did not make the payments required to retain the us e of those services.

rules.title: Eviction cause: disorderly conduct
rules.requirement: The landlord may file for eviction if, after a written Notice to Cease, the tenant continues disorderly conduct that destroys the peace and quiet of other tenants or the neighborhood. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: If after given written Notice to Cease disorderly conduct, the tenant continues the disorderly conduct and that conduct destroys the peace and quiet of the other tenants living in the building or neighborhood, the landlord may file a suite for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(b)).

rules.title: Eviction cause: damage or destruction to the property
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted for intentionally or through gross negligence causing or allowing destruction, damage or injury to the property. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: The tenant may be evicted if they have intentionally or by reason of gross negligence caused or allowed destruction, damage, or injury to the property.

rules.title: Eviction cause: substantial violation of landlord's rules and regulations
rules.requirement: After a written Notice to Cease, a tenant who continues to substantially violate reasonable rules in the lease or accepted in writing may be sued for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing, and notices must be given on or before the start of a new month.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction. In addition, any notices must be given on or before the start of a new month (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(d)).

rules.title: Eviction cause: breach of lease covenants
rules.requirement: If the tenant continues to substantially breach reasonable lease covenants after a written Notice to Cease and the lease reserves a right of re-entry, the landlord may file for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Leases in which the landlord has reserved a right of re-entry.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for this type of eviction.

rules.title: Eviction cause: public housing lease breach involving drugs or illegal activity
rules.requirement: In public housing, the landlord may file for eviction if the tenant substantially breached lease covenants about illegal drug use or other illegal activities; the covenant must conform to federal guidelines and be in effect at the start of the lease. No Notice to Cease is required; the Notice to Quit follows federal public housing regulations.
rules.quoted_span: 2) In public housing, if the tenant has substantially violated or breached any of the covenants or agreements contained in the lease, pertaining to illegal uses of controlled dangerous substances, or other illegal activities, the landlord may file a suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction cause: failure to pay rent increase
rules.requirement: If a tenant fails to pay rent after notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, the landlord may file for eviction; the increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with other laws including rent control. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: If a tenant fails to pay rent after being given notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, the landlord may file a suit for eviction.
rules.interaction_text: must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control

rules.title: Rent increase must not be unconscionable
rules.requirement: A rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control. A tenant who believes an increase is unconscionable may withhold the difference between the old and new rent, and the court decides.
rules.quoted_span: The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.
rules.interaction_text: must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control

rules.title: Eviction cause: health and safety violations or removal from rental market
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted where the landlord must board up or demolish for substantial violations, cannot abate violations with the tenant present, must correct an illegal occupancy, or a government agency removes the property from the rental market. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three months before filing, and the tenant cannot be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three months before filing
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit for eviction. The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for illegal occupancy evictions
rules.requirement: A tenant evicted for illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times the monthly rent, paid by the landlord at least five days before removal. If unpaid and no municipal fund exists, interest accrues at 18% per year and the amount due is a lien on the property.
rules.key_value: six times the tenant’s monthly rent
rules.coverage_text: Tenants evicted under cause G 3) (illegal occupancy).
rules.penalty: Interest accrues on the unpaid balance at the rate of 18% per year; the amount due is a lien on the property; landlord must repay the municipality's relocation fund.
rules.quoted_span: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.

rules.title: Eviction cause: permanent retirement from residential use
rules.requirement: A landlord who wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use may file for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served at least 18 months before filing, and no action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least 18 months prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Buildings or mobile home parks being permanently retired from residential use.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where the circumstances in section (G) apply.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months prior to filing the suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction cause: refusal to accept reasonable lease changes
rules.requirement: At lease expiration, if the tenant refuses reasonable but substantial changes after written notice, the landlord may file for eviction and the court decides reasonableness. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month before filing
rules.quoted_span: If after written notice the tenant refuses to accept those changes the landlord may file a suit for eviction and the court will determine if the proposed changes are reasonable.

rules.title: Eviction cause: continual nonpayment or habitual late payment
rules.requirement: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late after a written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month before filing
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

rules.title: Eviction cause: conversion to condominium, cooperative or fee simple
rules.requirement: A landlord converting a building or mobile home park to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may file for eviction after complying with conversion regulations; a Notice to Quit must be served at least three years before filing and no action until the lease expires. Courts may grant up to five one-year stays, and no action may be brought against protected senior citizen or disabled tenants.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three years before filing
rules.coverage_text: Buildings or mobile home parks being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership of two or more units or sites.
rules.exemptions: No action against a senior citizen or disabled tenant with protected tenancy status under the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be ser ved on the tenant at least three years before filing a suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction cause: post-conversion tenancy, sale to owner-occupant
rules.requirement: The owner of a building constructed as or converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple may evict a tenant whose tenancy began after the master deed was recorded when the unit is sold to a buyer who will occupy it, only if the tenant was given a statement that the property is being converted. A Notice to Quit must be served at least two months before filing, and no action until the lease expires.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least two months prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants whose initial tenancy began after the master deed, cooperative agreement or subdivision plat was recorded.
rules.quoted_span: However, no action shall be brought against a tenant under paragraph one (1) of this subsection unless the tenant was given a statement, informing the tenant that the property is being converted.

rules.title: Eviction cause: owner of three or fewer condo/co-op units seeking occupancy or sale
rules.requirement: An owner of three or less condominium or cooperative units may evict a tenant whose tenancy began after the master deed was recorded, to personally occupy the unit or sell it vacant to an occupying buyer. A Notice to Quit must be served at least two months before filing, and no action until the lease expires.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least two months prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Owners of three or less condominium or cooperative units, tenancies begun after the master deed or cooperative agreement was recorded.
rules.quoted_span: 2) The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of three or less condominium or cooperative units seeks to evict a tenant whose initial tenancy began, by rental, after the master deed or agreement establishing the cooperative was recorded, because the owner seeks to personally occupy the unit, or has contracted to sell the unit to a buyer who seeks to personally occupy it and the contract for sale calls for the unit to be vacant at the time of closing.

rules.title: Eviction cause: owner of building with three or fewer units seeking occupancy or sale
rules.requirement: The owner of a building with three residential units or less may evict to personally occupy a unit or to sell it vacant to a buyer who will occupy it. A Notice to Quit must be served at least two months before filing, and no action until the lease expires.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least two months prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Buildings with three residential units or less.
rules.quoted_span: 3) The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of a building with three residential units or less seeks to personally occupy a unit, or has contracted to sell the residential unit to a buyer who wishes to personally occupy it and the contract fo r sale calls for the unit to be vacant at the time of closing.

rules.title: Eviction cause: termination of employment-based tenancy
rules.requirement: If a tenant's occupancy is conditioned on employment by the landlord (e.g., superintendent or janitor) and that employment ends, the landlord may file for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit three days prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants residing on the condition of employment by the landlord.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

rules.title: Eviction cause: drug offense conviction on the property
rules.requirement: The landlord may file for eviction if the tenant was convicted of or pleaded guilty to drug offenses on the property and has not completed or is not participating in a drug rehabilitation program, or lets such a person occupy the premises; suits must be brought within two years. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to a tenant allowing a juvenile found delinquent due to use or possession of drugs to reside at the property.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(n)).

rules.title: Eviction cause: assault or terrorist threats against landlord, family or employees
rules.requirement: The landlord may file for eviction if the tenant was convicted of, pleaded guilty to, or a juvenile was found delinquent for assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, family or employees, or the tenant knowingly lets such a person reside there; suits must be brought within two years. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to, or if a juvenile has been found by the court to be delinquent due to an offense involving assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, a member of the landl ord’s family or an employee of the landlord.

rules.title: Eviction cause: civil liability for criminal activities
rules.requirement: The landlord may file for eviction if a civil court finds the tenant liable for theft on the premises, assaults or terrorist threats against the landlord, family or employees, or illegal drug activities on the premises (without rehabilitation), or the tenant knowingly lets such a person reside there; suits must be brought within two years. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to a tenant allowing a juvenile found delinquent due to the use or possession of drugs to reside at the property.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(p)).

rules.title: Eviction cause: conviction for theft of property
rules.requirement: The landlord may file for eviction if the tenant was convicted of, pleaded guilty to, or a juvenile was found delinquent for theft from the landlord or other tenants in the building or complex, or the tenant knowingly lets such a person reside there. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(q)).

rules.title: Eviction cause: human trafficking
rules.requirement: The landlord may file for eviction if the tenant is found in a civil action to have committed human trafficking on the premises or knowingly harbors or permits a person engaged in human trafficking to occupy the premises. No action may be brought more than two years after the violation has terminated.
rules.quoted_span: No action for removal pursuant to this subsection may be brought mor e than two years after the alleged violation has terminated (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(r)).

rules.title: Evictions in owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only by court order on listed causes (holdover, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, damage, rule violations, lease breach with re-entry). A three-month notice to quit is required for at-will or year-to-year tenancies, one month for month-to-month and other tenancies, and three days for disorderly, destructive or rule-violation causes; none for nonpayment.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction.

rules.title: Rooming and boarding house evictions
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless otherwise ordered by the Bureau. They must also give at least three (3) working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting an eviction action.
rules.key_value: at least three (3) working days’ notice to the County Welfare Board
rules.coverage_text: Rooming and boarding houses: buildings with at least two living units occupied by unrelated persons without private kitchens and bathrooms, unless an exception in the Rooming and Boarding House Act applies.
rules.exemptions: Except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau; buildings meeting an exception in the Rooming and Boarding House Act.
rules.quoted_span: The Regulations Governing Rooming and Boarding Houses, which are enforced by the Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards of the Department of Community Affairs, require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau (N.J.A.C. 5:27-3.3(c)).
